```{python}
from step1_prepare_image import prepare_image
from step2_create_stipple import create_stipple
from step3_create_tonal import create_tonal
from step4_create_block_letter import create_block_letter_s
from step5_create_masked import create_masked_stipple
from create_meme import create_statistics_meme

original_img = prepare_image("CP3A9906.JPG")
stipple_img, samples = create_stipple(original_img)
tonal_img, average_tones, stats = create_tonal(original_img)
height, width = original_img.shape
block_letter_img = create_block_letter_s(height, width)
masked_stipple_img = create_masked_stipple(stipple_img, block_letter_img)
create_statistics_meme(
    original_img=original_img,
    stipple_img=stipple_img,
    block_letter_img=block_letter_img,
    masked_stipple_img=masked_stipple_img,
    output_path="statistics_meme.png"
)
```
```{python}
#| output: true
from IPython.display import Image
Image("statistics_meme.png")
```

This meme demonstrates selection bias by showing how systematic missing data patterns distort our understanding of reality. The original image (Reality) represents the true population, while the stippled version (Your Model) shows how we collect data. When selection bias removes data points in a systematic "S" pattern, the resulting estimate no longer represents the true population — just like in real-world studies where missing data leads to wrong conclusions.
